clue.text: Go wrong, being behind, getting sack

parts.note: being at the rear of something is being at the back
to sack an employee is to fire them

explanation.surface: Someone falls behind at work and is sacked, so everything goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that backfires misfires and produces the opposite of the intended result.

clue.text: Counter-strike

explanation.surface: A retaliatory blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffet is a refreshment counter, and to buffet is to strike repeatedly.

clue.text: Crown for a smoker

explanation.surface: A crown made for someone who smokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Corona is Latin for crown, and a corona is a long straight-sided cigar.

clue.text: Sack member for producing a gun

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: An employee is fired for bringing a gun to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm is a portable weapon such as a rifle or pistol.

clue.text: Tea, perhaps, in the garden

parts.note: not a drink taken outdoors but a garden flower of which the tea variety is one kind

explanation.definitionFit: The tea is a variety of this flowering shrub, grown in gardens.

clue.text: Lick the top off and attempt to hold it? Not so easy!

indicators.note: the word for attempt is told to hold the trimmed lick within itself

parts.note: an attempt is a try

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, so lick loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: Advice on eating an ice cream: lick off the top and try to keep hold of it, which is harder than it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lick' looks like an instruction about ice cream; with 'the top off' it loses its first letter, and 'to hold it' sets the remainder inside the attempt word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tricky is awkward or difficult, the opposite of simple.

clue.text: Computer data to be delivered verbally?

explanation.surface: A computer printout that is to be spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A readout is information displayed by a computer, and something said to an audience from a text is spoken from the page.

clue.text: Director's new role?

indicators.note: a new role, read as a new roll, means the letters of the company boss are rolled into fresh order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A company director taking up a different position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new role' rearranges DIRECTOR; the whole clue suggests what a director becomes when owed money.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditor is someone owed money, a role a director takes on when lending to the company.

clue.text: The oldest converse

parts.note: converse is used as a noun: the opposite of the eldest, the least aged one

explanation.definitionFit: The least aged member of a family is the opposite of the eldest.

clue.text: Strong point in favour of a lock, apparently

parts.note: being in favour of something is being for it
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: An argument for a particular lock, presented as its strongest feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong point' reads as an advantage; here it is a military stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress is a fortified place, a stronghold or military strong point.

clue.text: Strong point in favour of a lock, apparently (8) 10It is consumed in a province of Germany

definitions.text: It is consumed in a province of Germany

indicators.note: the eating word is placed in the middle of the German province

parts.note: a Gau was a historical German district or province
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: Something eaten in a German region, the whole clue describing a rich cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR ran 9-across's clue into this one; the clue proper is 'It is consumed in a province of Germany', and the whole of it also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich cake, something eaten, and Black Forest gateau comes from a German region.

clue.text: Vocal accompaniment some French are unable to follow

parts.note: des means some in French
are unable means can't, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A singing part some French people cannot keep up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' links the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A descant is a melody sung above the main tune, a vocal counterpoint.

clue.text: Nine in a group need an excursion

indicators.note: an excursion is a wandering out, so these letters go off on a rearranging trip

explanation.surface: A party of nine people needs a day out.
explanation.definitionFit: An ennead is a set or group of nine, from the Greek word for nine.

clue.text: Changing into something that suits you

explanation.surface: A change of outfit into something flattering.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning into describes a process of transformation, while flattering clothing is said to look good on its wearer.

clue.text: Showed delight at direction into hard work

indicators.note: the direction is placed inside the hard work word

parts.note: a grind is tedious hard work
NE is northeast, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone smiled at being directed to a tough job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who grinned smiled broadly in pleasure.

clue.text: A broken promise, it can lead to bad language

indicators.note: a broken promise is shattered, so its letters together with the next two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Breaking a promise can provoke a stream of swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges PROMISE and IT CAN; the opening 'A' and 'lead to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprecations are curses or oaths, the sort of swearing called bad language.

clue.text: Offered carrot top for a tease-made to take it down

indicators.note: to tease wool or hair is to comb it out, so the letters are teased apart and rearranged
the top of the word carrot is its first letter

explanation.surface: A carrot offered as a tease to someone made to swallow it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' takes C from 'carrot', and 'for a tease' rearranges it with OFFERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone force-fed is compelled to eat, made to swallow food against their will.

clue.text: After the panic, sailor gets something to eat

parts.note: a flap is a state of panic
Jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: After a panic, a sailor gets a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just keeps the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A flapjack is an oat bar in Britain, or a pancake in America: food either way.

clue.text: Compelling the head to show courtesy

parts.note: obliging someone to do something is compelling them
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Forcing the boss to behave politely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like a person in charge; it is a headland, NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Obligingness is willingness to help others, a kind of politeness or good manners.

clue.text: Big fish just too big for our foreign friend

annotationWithheld.why: Big fish just too big for our foreign friend: OUR + AMI (our French friend) gives OURAMI, but no clue word soundly supplies the extra G; 'just too big' only hints at one letter more
annotationWithheld.clue: Big fish just too big for our foreign friend

clue.text: Tank holding green stuff

parts.note: salad is green leafy food
a container holding something has it in, so holding gives in

explanation.surface: A tank of water with greenery growing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tank' is not a water tank but an armoured vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saladin was a British armoured car of the 1950s, a tank-like fighting vehicle.

clue.text: Force used to be wrong

parts.note: ex means former, what used to be
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Force that was once used is condemned as wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To extort is to obtain by force or threats, as in forcing money from someone.

clue.text: Vessel overturned chap on it sees sea- monster

indicators.note: in a down clue the vessel is turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: an ark is a vessel, as in Noah's ark
Ken is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: A man on a capsized boat spots a sea monster.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'overturned' means read upwards; 'on it sees' are link words joining the boat and the chap to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The kraken is a legendary giant sea creature of Norse folklore.

clue.text: With these containers there's less movement on top, going round a bend

parts.note: a top for a bottle is a cap

indicators.note: the reshuffled letters encircle the bend letter
movement of the letters of less means they are shifted into a new order

parts.note: a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter U

explanation.surface: Advice that a capped container will spill less when going round a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' looks like part of the sentence but is anagram fodder; 'movement' scrambles it and 'going round' wraps it around the bend letter, all placed under the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsules are small sealed cases or containers, such as those holding medicine.

clue.text: Nine lire may be given for a fabulous drink

indicators.note: the letters may be given a new arrangement, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Paying nine lire for a wonderful drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be given' rearranges IX with LIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a legendary potion, such as the elixir of life, a drink found in fables.

clue.text: Had mashed. up then left the food

indicators.note: mashed food is crushed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone had mashed food then left it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mashed' rearranges HAD to DHA; 'up then' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Dhal is an Indian dish of spiced lentils.

clue.text: A scarf that's knotted may bring trouble

indicators.note: a knotted scarf is twisted up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A badly knotted scarf could cause an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy disturbance or brawl, a bout of trouble.

clue.text: Fruit and fish from the south

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south
a haddock is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A grocer's order of fruit and fish from the south of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the south' looks like where the fish was caught; it puts S at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaddock is a large citrus fruit, also called the pomelo.

clue.text: A couple of youngsters back one animal

indicators.note: back means the doubled word is read from right to left
a couple means two, so the young goat word is written twice

parts.note: a kid is a youngster

explanation.surface: Two children backing a particular animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A couple of' doubles KID to KIDKID, and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The dik-dik is a tiny African antelope.

clue.text: Board attaching considerable weight to an infinitesimal matter at sea

parts.note: a plank is a board of wood
a ton is a large unit of weight

explanation.surface: A heavy weight tied to a board at sea, out of all proportion to a tiny matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton are the minute drifting organisms in the sea.
